options: A single firewall rule that blocks all inbound internet traffic
A technique for compressing network packets to save bandwidth
A way to merge multiple subnets into one flat trusted network
Breaking a network into many small, individually secured segments instead of one large trusted zone
questions.explain: Microsegmentation replaces one large trusted zone with many narrow, individually secured segments, each scoped to a specific workload.

questions.q: What is "lateral movement," and why does microsegmentation target it?
options: A type of encryption used to protect data in transit
The process of migrating a VM between Azure regions
An attacker moving from one compromised system to others on the same network; microsegmentation contains the breach to one segment
A method for load-balancing traffic evenly across servers
questions.explain: Microsegmentation's main goal is containment — stopping a compromised workload from freely reaching every other workload on the network.

questions.q: How does a microsegmented NSG rule differ from a perimeter-style, subnet-wide rule?
options: It only applies to traffic leaving the virtual network, never traffic inside it
It removes the need for any security rules at all
It names the exact source, destination, and port a specific workload tier is allowed to use, rather than allowing broad any-to-any traffic
It requires replacing NSGs with an entirely different tool
questions.explain: Microsegmentation doesn't introduce new tools — it scopes the same NSGs and Security Groups far more tightly, per workload rather than per subnet.

questions.q: What does "deny-by-default" mean in a microsegmented network?
options: All traffic is allowed unless a rule explicitly blocks it
No traffic is allowed between segments unless a rule explicitly permits it
Deny-by-default only applies to north-south traffic, never east-west
Only traffic from outside the network is denied; internal traffic is unrestricted
questions.explain: A microsegmented network starts from deny-by-default — east-west traffic between segments is blocked unless explicitly allowed.

questions.q: What advantage do Azure Application Security Groups add on top of NSGs?
options: They let you group VMs by role (web, app, database) and write rules against that role instead of an IP range
They are only usable for traffic crossing the internet edge
They replace the need for any NSG rules entirely
They automatically encrypt all east-west traffic
questions.explain: Application Security Groups let a rule target a workload's role rather than a subnet's IP range, so it keeps working as individual machines come and go.
